content.value_statement: Long agent sessions can waste tokens, slow responses, and lose important context. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical methods for compression, masking, caching, and partitioning.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to compact, mask, cache, or partition context.
Provides heuristics for token budgets and optimization trigger points.
Includes Python utilities for token estimation, summarization, masking, and budget tracking.
Shows cache-friendly prompt ordering patterns for stable prefixes.
Guides multi-agent partitioning and result aggregation for large tasks.
limitations: Token counting uses rough estimates unless a production tokenizer is added.
Example summarizers are heuristic and may miss domain-specific details.
The skill provides guidance and sample utilities, not a hosted optimization service.
KV-cache results depend on the model provider and inference infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Control Long Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Apply compaction and observation masking when tool outputs dominate the context window.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers using Claude Code or Codex

use_cases.title: Reduce Production Agent Costs
use_cases.description: Set token budgets, optimization triggers, and cache-friendly prompt structures for repeated workloads.

use_cases.title: Partition Large Research Tasks
use_cases.description: Split broad work across focused sub-agents and merge results without carrying every detail forward.

prompt_templates.title: Find Context Waste
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of a long conversation or workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this workflow for context waste. Identify repeated outputs, stale messages, and content that can be summarized or masked.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Token Budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a repeatable agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context budget for this agent workflow. Allocate tokens by system prompt, tools, retrieved documents, history, outputs, and reserve buffer.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cache-Friendly Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt design for repeated requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Reorder this prompt structure to maximize KV-cache reuse. Keep stable content first and move dynamic fields near the end.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Partitioning Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-agent decomposition for large tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a context partitioning plan for this task. Define sub-agent scopes, context boundaries, output contracts, and aggregation checks.

output_examples.input: A coding session with repeated test logs, old command output, and a nearly full context window.
output: Compact old decisions into a short session summary.
Mask repeated test logs behind references after key failures are captured.
Keep the current bug, latest stack trace, and active file list visible.

output_examples.input: A production agent that answers similar support questions with changing customer details.
output: Place policy, tool definitions, and response rules before customer-specific data.
Move timestamps, account details, and request identifiers near the end.
Track cache hit rate and revise unstable prompt sections.

output_examples.input: A research workflow with many documents and separate analysis threads.
output: Assign focused sub-agents to document groups.
Require concise findings with citations and unresolved questions.
Merge compatible results and summarize conflicts before final synthesis.

best_practices: Measure context usage before choosing an optimization method.
Preserve current task facts, decisions, and unresolved questions during compaction.
Keep stable prompt elements first to improve cache reuse across similar requests.
anti_patterns: Masking recent observations that are still needed for active reasoning.
Adding timestamps or session identifiers near the beginning of repeated prompts.
Partitioning work without clear output contracts and aggregation checks.

faq.question: Does this skill increase the model context window?
faq.answer: No. It helps use the available context window more efficiently through compression, masking, caching, and partitioning.

faq.question: Can it reduce token costs?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on reducing repeated, stale, or low-value context while preserving important task information.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository includes Python examples for token estimation, compaction, observation masking, budgets, and cache metrics.

faq.question: Is it specific to Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: It is compatible with all three. Some implementation details depend on the model provider and tool environment.

faq.question: When should observation masking be used?
faq.answer: Use it for verbose outputs that have already served their purpose and can be retrieved or summarized later.

faq.question: What should never be compacted?
faq.answer: Do not compact system instructions, active task requirements, recent critical evidence, or unresolved decisions needed for the current step.
